findings.title: Unhandled nil TopicUser causes 500 error in unsubscribe action
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (e.g. a user who navigates directly to the unsubscribe URL for a topic they were never notified about or that never created a topic_user row). The following lines immediately call `tu.notification_level` and `tu.save!` without a nil check, which will raise `NoMethodError` and produce an unhandled 500 error instead of a graceful response.

findings.title: State-changing action exposed via GET request (CSRF exposure)
findings.body: The `unsubscribe` action mutates persistent state (changes `TopicUser#notification_level`) but is routed as a GET endpoint (`config/routes.rb`: `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`). Rails' CSRF protection by default only guards unsafe (non-GET) verbs, so this endpoint is not covered by CSRF tokens. Any third party page can trigger this mutation for a logged-in user simply by causing their browser to issue a GET to this URL (e.g. via an `` tag, link prefetching, or crawler), silently changing/muting their topic notification settings without consent.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url but is not validated
findings.body: `config/locales/server.en.yml`'s `unsubscribe_link` string was changed to embed `%{unsubscribe_url}`, and `MessageBuilder#html_part`/`#body` render it via `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true. There is no guard ensuring `unsubscribe_url` is present in `template_args` for every caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Any current or future caller (mailer or plugin) that enables `add_unsubscribe_link` without supplying `unsubscribe_url` will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` at email-build time, breaking that notification entirely.

findings.title: Template path inconsistent with flat route/controller naming, may fail to resolve
findings.body: The new route is registered with a flat name `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', ...)` in app-route-map.js.es6, and its controller/view are placed using the matching flat naming convention (`controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`). However the template was placed in a nested path `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` instead of the flat `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`. Under the classic Ember resolver conventions used elsewhere in this codebase, a flat route name resolves to a flat (dasherized) template name, not a nested directory path. This mismatch risks the template not being found/resolved for the `topicUnsubscribe` route, resulting in a blank or broken unsubscribe page.

findings.title: Misspelled property name 'stopNotificiationsText'
findings.body: The computed property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (missing an 'a', should be `stopNotificationsText`). It's used consistently in the matching template (`{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}`) so it functions, but the typo will confuse future maintainers and complicate searching/refactoring this code.

findings.title: No test coverage verifying the unsubscribe_url is actually rendered in the email
findings.body: The test fixture `message_with_unsubscribe` now passes `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"`, but none of the existing assertions check that this URL is actually interpolated into the rendered `unsubscribe_link` text/body/html_part. The only assertion reused (`has the user preferences url in the body`) predates this change and does not exercise the new per-topic unsubscribe link behavior, so a regression in the `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation (e.g. missing argument errors, or the URL simply not appearing) would not be caught by this spec.

findings.title: No controller specs added for the new unsubscribe action
findings.body: The PR introduces a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action with non-trivial branching logic (slug mismatch redirect, notification level toggling between muted/regular/tracking/watching, nil-handling risk noted separately), and a new `Topic#unsubscribe_url` helper, but no new or updated controller/model specs were added to verify this behavior (e.g. correct notification level transitions, redirect behavior on slug mismatch, response format handling).
